w: Grade II* listed and holding one of the largest art collections in England outside London, the Walker is the grand dame of National Museums Liverpool - proof this port city's wealth bought more than warehouses. No single blockbuster draws the crowds; the depth of the permanent collection is the real hook.
s: One of England's biggest art collections outside London
_facts: Grade II* listed art gallery in Liverpool
Houses one of the largest art collections in England outside London
Part of the National Museums Liverpool group

w: Grade I listed twice over - church and hall both - this Sefton Park Unitarian chapel quietly made history as the first UK place of worship to register a civil partnership for a same-sex couple. A radical footnote hiding behind solid Victorian stonework.
s: First UK church to register a same-sex civil partnership
_facts: Unitarian church at 57 Ullet Road, Sefton Park, Liverpool
Church and attached hall are both separately Grade I listed
First place of worship in the UK to register a civil partnership for a same-sex couple
Member of the General Assembly of Unitarian and Free Christian Churches

w: George Frederick Bodley's Grade I masterpiece at Tuebrook is exceptional enough on its own - the vicarage and mortuary house he also designed are both Grade II listed too - but the real pull is Brockman Memorial Hall next door, one of the Beatles' earliest venues.
s: Grade I Bodley church with an early Beatles venue next door
_facts: Active Anglican parish church in the Diocese of Liverpool, Tuebrook
Built in the 1860s, designed by George Frederick Bodley
Grade I listed as a building of exceptional architectural interest
Vicarage and mortuary house on site, also by Bodley, both Grade II listed
Site of the Brockman Memorial Hall, an early venue of the Beatles

w: One of only four WWII German U-boats preserved anywhere in the world - and the only one cut into sections for display. U-534 sank no ships in her short training career before an RAF bomber caught her in the Kattegat in 1945; salvaged in 1993, she resurfaced at Birkenhead's Woodside Ferry as the 'U-Boat Story.'
s: One of only four preserved WWII German U-boats
_facts: Type IXC/40 U-boat of Nazi Germany's Kriegsmarine, built 1942
One of only four preserved WWII German submarines in the world, and the only one cut into sections
Used mainly for training; sank no ships during her service
Sunk by an RAF bomber on 5 May 1945 in the Kattegat near Anholt, Denmark
Salvaged in 1993 and moved to Woodside Ferry, Birkenhead, forming the 'U-Boat Story' museum (opened 2009, closed 2020)
